findings.problem: The "cost" explanation gives a reason the text doesn't give: "He says it twice so nobody walks up to the counter still digging for a wallet." Isaiah 55:1 doesn't say why the LORD repeats "without money." He can point out the repetition, but not give a reason for it.

rule.text: Reasons. He never adds why someone did, said or thought something unless the text says why.

findings.problem: This card is the first time David, Moses and Abraham come up, but no explanation says who they are. The "David" explanation just uses the name; something like "David, Israel's king" is needed. The "Moses" and "Abraham" explanations name those men without saying who they are either.

rule.text: New people. The first time someone shows up, he says simply who they are, like "Cyrus, king of Persia" or "Moses, Israel's leader."

findings.problem: The "Abraham" explanation says "Then verse 4 keeps the spotlight on David." That is a bare reference, with nothing from the verse brought in.

rule.text: He explains. He brings in the verse when it helps, and it flows naturally in what he says. Never a reference on its own.

findings.problem: The "David" explanation ends with "When God puts loving devotion on a promise with your name on it, friend, that's a box nobody's unsealing." "Your name" makes it sound like the baker's name is on the promise, when the name on it is David's. A sealed cookie box is also a finished, good thing in his world, so "nobody's unsealing" doesn't clearly mean "unbreakable." A stranger would say "huh?"

rule.text: If a stranger would say "huh?", rewrite it.

findings.problem: The explanations follow a visible template. Missed answers nearly always open by praising the guess and then pivot with "friend, but" ("I like where your head's at, friend", "Moses is a strong guess, friend, but", "Abraham is a solid guess, friend, but", "I can see the logic, friend", "That's a tender guess, friend, but"). Almost every explanation then says "In Isaiah 55:N the LORD says" and the same quote. On several cards every answer uses the same lead-in and the same quote word for word: stop 1 card 2 (all three quote "Come, buy wine and milk without money and without cost!" after "in Isaiah 55:1 the LORD says"), stop 1 card 4, stop 1 card 10 (all three), stop 2 card 5 ("higher" and "older"), stop 2 card 8 (both) and stop 2 card 14 ("everlasting" and "hidden"). Moses and Abraham on stop 1 card 7 have almost the same opening.

rule.text: There is no formula. Each explanation sounds natural and different from the others.
